Money in the Bank takes place in New Orleans on Oct. 10

        There is no rest for the weary. Moments after successfully defending the world heavyweight championship against Penta in Mexico City, Roman Reigns suffered LA Knight's wrath. Now, Reigns and Knight meet at Money in the Bank.For years, WWE fans have clamored for Knight to win the Money in the Bank briefcase. He won't get that opportunity because he's challenging for Monday Night Raw's top prize. Knight's issues with The Bloodline have persisted for months. In New Orleans, he gets another chance to strike Reigns and collect his first WWE world title.The Money in the Bank event is largely fleshed out. Its two titular ladder matches have a full field. The men's division has a very competitive bracket. One could make a legitimate argument for CM Punk, Kevin Owens, Bron Breakker, Trick Williams or Penta winning the briefcase. The women's field includes Tiffany Stratton, a former briefcase holder, along with Lash Legend and Sol Ruca.Take a look below at the confirmed matches for Money in the Bank and take a glance at the crystal ball of what may come. The event streams live on ESPN Unlimited on Oct. 10, with the main card starting at 6 p.m. ET.2026 WWE Money in the Bank matchesWorld Heavyweight Championship -- Roman Reigns (c) vs. LA Knight: After a memorable match between Reigns and Penta in Mexico City, Knight sprung an attack on the world heavyweight champion. It was a stern reminder that the title defense with Penta was a brief detour, and that Knight had unfinished business with the champ. Once Raw concluded, WWE confirmed Reigns vs. Knight for Money in the Bank.
Money in the Bank Ladder Match -- Bron Breakker vs. Je'Von Evans vs. Penta vs. Trick Williams vs. CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens: Triple threat qualifying matches determine this year's Money in the Bank competitors. Breakker beat Rey Mysterio and Ethan Page to qualify. Evans punched his ticket by overcoming Big Cass and Austin Theory. Penta, who replaced Solo Sikoa, beat Dominik Mysterio and Dragon Lee to qualify. Williams joined the fray after upsetting Randy Orton and Rey Fenix. The most high-profile inclusion in the match is two-time briefcase holder Punk, who beat Finn Balor and Gunther. Owens secured the final spot after quelling Johnny Gargano's spirited performance, although Owens should thank Randy Orton for removing Cody Rhodes from the equation.Money in the Bank Ladder Match -- Sol Ruca vs. Lola Vice vs. Roxanne Perez vs. Jacy Jayne vs. Lash Legend vs. Tiffany Stratton: Ruca and Vice were the first two participants confirmed for the women's ladder match. Ruca beat former women's intercontinental champions Lyra Valkyria and Maxxine Dupri. Vice followed that up by edging out NXT women's champion Kelani Jordan and WWE women's intercontinental champion Raquel Rodriguez. Then Perez beat Iyo Sky and La Catalina to qualify. Jayne and Legend captured the next two spots. The final slot went to Tiffany Stratton, who beat Candice LeRae and Tatum Paxley.Oba Femi vs. Bronson Reed: Who is the biggest, baddest man on Raw? WWE fans will soon find out. Femi has had his fair share of problems with The Vision lately. At Money in the Bank, he'll get Reed, the group's powerhouse, all to himself. 
WWE Women's World Championship -- Stephanie Vaquer (c) vs. Liv Morgan or Becky Lynch: There's a three-superstar rivalry brewing on Raw. With the rivalry brewing and no clear title challenger, Lynch and Morgan will wrestle each other for the right to face Vaquer.

The action heats up on Saturday night in Los Angeles and there's plenty of ways to get in on it

        UFC 332 goes down on Saturday from Salt Lake City, and the card is an interesting one, headlined by a bout between Natalia Silva and Wang Cong for the vacant women's flyweight championship.After longtime dominant women's flyweight queen Valentina Shevchenko suffered an injury that will keep her sidelined for at least a year, she was forced to vacate the title. With UFC 332 in need of a headliner, Silva and Cong were paired to crown a new champion in Shevchenko's absence.One of the main attractions for Saturday lands in the co-main event where rising star Payton Talbott makes his return. The young bantamweight hoped for a more active 2026, but he says that potential fights with fellow Americans like Sean O'Malley fell through, leaving him to wait until now for his expected lone fight of the year. He draws a tough customer in Deiveson Figueiredo, the former two-time flyweight champion. Figueiredo has struggled a bit with age and now up at 135 pounds, but he's always a tough out.You can watch UFC 332 live on CBS this Saturday beginning at 8 p.m. ET. The action is also available on Paramount+ -- along with every other UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
With such an interesting card set for UFC 332, there will no doubt be plenty of interest in the event, including at sportsbooks. With that in mind, we've once again looked at all the event's main card fights to identify our best bets for each.
        
            
                UFC 332: Payton Talbott eyes busy 2027 after Sean O'Malley, Cory Sandhagen fights failed to materialize
                
                    Shakiel Mahjouri                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
After a rough 1-3 result for our best bets for UFC 331, we are sitting at 22-24 for the year. Now we look ahead to this weekend with the goal of getting back in the black, with our only rule remaining that all bets must be at odds of -250 or better. Let's take a look at this week's picks with odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.Ateba Gautier	vs.	Roman KopylovOver 1.5 rounds (-155)Ateba Gautier is a scary man. He has finished almost all of his wins (9 of 11 career, four of five UFC), but he faces the biggest test of his career in Roman Kopylov. What makes Kopylov such an interesting opponent for Gautier isn't just his 12 Octagon appearances, but the fact that he has never been stopped by strikes in his career. In five career losses, Kopylov has twice lost by submission and three times by decision. There's a chance that Gautier's power striking wears down Kopylov, just as there's a chance Kopylov's endurance can contribute to wearing Gautier down and allowing him to take over the fight as it goes along. Because of that uncertainty, we'll instead rely on Kopylov's durability dragging this fight into the second half, and Kopylov only having been under 1.5 rounds once in his UFC career only makes the line more appealing.
Roberto Soldic vs.	Khaos WilliamsRoberto Soldic via KO/TKO/DQ (-150)I don't love the line here, but it's the one I'm most comfortable with that fits our -250 or better rule. The Soldic moneyline is sitting at -260 and I do think he has exactly the right game to beat Williams, who has had some rough times against the better competition he has faced. Soldic has multiple professional boxing knockouts and 18 of his 21 pro wins in MMA have come by KO or TKO. Williams absorbs 5.34 strikes per minute, which is too many to take against someone who hits as hard as Soldic.King Green	vs.	Esteban RibovicsKing Green moneyline (+190)I'm a bit baffled by the line here. It has come back toward Green a bit in recent days, but there is still a lot of value on Green. Ribovics is explosive and throws strikes with abandon, but Green is a more efficient, more defensively disciplined fighter whose striking skills are applied in such a way that he still lands plenty without needing to provide the same kind of defensive holes as Ribovics. I think the odds could be completely flipped and arguably would make more sense than they do as they currently stand. Green is riding a four-fight winning streak, and the two-fight losing skid that came before that streak doesn't look too bad given where Mauricio Ruffy and Paddy Pimblett stand in the division. Take Green's more disciplined style here.Deiveson Figueiredo	vs.	Payton TalbottPayton Talbott via decision (+140)Talbott's loss to Raoni Barcelos was jarring, for sure. He was a massive favorite that night and simply couldn't handle Barcelos' takedowns and ground game. For everything Figueiredo has accomplished in his career, his recent run at bantamweight has been rough. Figueiredo is tough as hell and isn't an easy out for anyone, but he didn't carry up a particularly scary amount of power, and he can't muscle anyone around at 135 pounds. Talbott will have the edge in size, power, reach and strength. That should set up a fight where Talbott gets to decide where things take place. If Talbott wants to use offensive wrestling as he did against Henry Cejudo, he should be able to do so. And if he wants to strike, he should have the ability to control the action there as well. However, Figueiredo's toughness makes getting to the final scorecards feel like a more than reasonable play.
Natalia Silva	vs.	Wang CongNatalia Silva via decision (-110)This is a very interesting fight, even if it feels odd for a main event spot on a "numbered event." Cong is an aggressive striker who hits hard and throws a ton of strikes. Silva also brings a striker-first mentality to the Octagon, but does so with more of a defensive mentality. Silva is perfect in the UFC and has won three straight fights over former champions, giving her the more proven resume of the two. Cong has suffered defeat in the UFC, she's had two fights at a catchweight, one of which was her fault, and she was deducted a point in her most recent fight. That's an interesting and kind of strange resume, which is always fun. That said, as long as Silva can remain patient and defensively responsible, she has the right style to slow Cong and edge out what I believe will be a narrow decision.Who wins Silva vs. Wang, and how exactly does the fight end? Visit SportsLine now to get detailed picks and analysis from the incomparable expert who is up over $21,000 on his UFC picks since May 2018, and find out.

Stroud and the rival Houston Texans. Quarterback Marcus Mariota again gets the start for the Commanders, as Jayden Daniels continues to ramp up after dislocating his elbow in Week 2 against the Dallas Cowboys. Daniels has not been placed on injured reserve and does not plan to have surgery right now. He was a limited participant in practice this week while sporting a brace on his left arm.As for the Colts, they are adjusting to life without Alec Pierce -- who was placed on injured reserve with his ankle injury. Josh Downs has stepped up in his place, catching 12 passes for 149 yards over the last two weeks. He will again be an important part of the game plan with Keenan Allen ruled out with a groin injury. Daniel Jones has thrown one touchdown and one interception in each game this year.         The Denver Broncos and San Francisco 49ers are facing off on CBS this Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET at Levi's Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, with Denver at 2-1, while the 49ers are one of the two undefeated NFC teams at 3-0. The 49ers started the season strong, defeating the Rams, who were a Super Bowl favorite heading into the season. They then defeated the Miami Dolphins and, most recently, took down the Arizona Cardinals.Denver began the year with a 31-10 divisional loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, then beat the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Los Angeles Rams.The Niners have been hit hard by injuries, which we'll get into more below, but they've shown they can adapt and win with whoever is on the field. Their offense is a fun one to watch — remember the hook-and-ladder that allowed for Deebo Samuel to have a stat line of 0 receptions for 80 yards and a touchdown?
The Broncos have demonstrated that they can come from behind and win, as they did last week against the Rams.Where to watch 49ers vs. BroncosDate: Sunday, Oct. 4 | Time: 4:25 p.m. ETLocation: Levi's Stadium (Santa Clara, CA)TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: 49ers -3 (via DraftKings)49ers vs. Broncos injuriesTo say the Niners have been hit hard by injuries is an understatement. Wide receivers Ricky Pearsall, Demarcus Robinson, Christian Kirk and De'Zhaun Stribling; tight end Jake Tonges; running back Isaac Guerendo; offensive linemen Austen Pleasants and Brett Toth; defensive ends Sam Okuayinonu, Mikail Kamara and Andrew Farmer II; defensive tackles Alfred Collins and CJ West; linebacker Nick Martin; defensive back Darrick Forrest and cornerback Nate Hobbs, to name a few, have all been on the injured reserve or PUP list.
There are so many players injured that the team has to strategically pick who they put on injured reserve so they don't run out of space, and that brings us to this week's injury report. They had 10 players on Wednesday's report, including Mykel Williams, who began the season on the PUP list. Defensive lineman Nick Bosa was listed with a knee/calf injury and is expected to miss multiple weeks. He is not on IR likely because the team doesn't have the space.Wide receivers Mike Evans (ribs) and KhaDarel Hodge (knee); linebacker Dre Greenlaw (quad); and defensive linemen James Thompson Jr. (ankle) and Keion White (hamstring) were all listed as non-participants in Wednesday and Thursday's practice. Running back Christian McCaffrey and tackle Trent Williams also did not practice on Wednesday, but were listed as "not injury related/resting player," and both returned as limited participants on Thursday.49ers vs. Broncos need to knowMVPurdy: Let's pretend it's not too soon to start talking about who the MVP will be and instead talk about why the 49ers quarterback is off to an MVP start. The definition of who the MVP is varies across the league and among fans every year, whether you think it's for the player who performed best overall or who meant the most to their team. Whichever way you slice it, Mr. Irrelevant, if we can still call him that, is in the conversation. He ranks eighth in passing yards (789), is tied for first in touchdown passes (9), second in completion percentage among current starters (72.3) and third in yards per attempt (10.2). He hasn't been sacked yet, and the challenge for the Broncos' defense is that it isn't quick to get to the QB. Denver's secondary is tough and can force turnovers, but the 49ers are quick to give the ball up.
The run game: The 49ers offense excels in the run game, and the Broncos defense doesn't excel in stopping the run. San Fran is sixth in rushing yards (409) and fourth in yards per carry (5.1). Denver's defense has allowed the third most yards (431) and is tied for the second-most yards per carry (5.1). Denver will need to even up this mismatch as much as possible, or the Niners will run all over them (pun intended). The Broncos' run game is not their offensive strong suit, with the second-fewest rushing yards (243) and the second-most fumbles (2). The Niners' run defense is in the middle of the pack. Who can establish the run, and who can establish it early, will be huge in the outcome of this game.49ers vs. Broncos predictionThe 49ers haven't given me a reason to believe they won't win this game, and while I think it will be competitive, I think they improve to 4-0. They have made it work with the number of injuries they're dealing with, but if the injury bug doesn't slow down soon, the holes will become more obvious than they are now.  Pick: 49ers

Facing the Jaguars will be a good temperature check to see where they rank among early AFC contenders. Cincinnati has the challenge of playing in a division with the 3-1 Cleveland Browns (who might just be good), 2-1 Baltimore Ravens and the Pittsburgh Steelers, who sit at .500 but came a few plays away from 3-1. Jacksonville, on the other hand, is the only AFC South team with a winning record. It shares the division with 1-2 Indianapolis and the winless Tennessee Titans and Houston Texans.
It's early in the season, but these two teams have real playoff possibilities, and this game could prove to be very meaningful when the postseason comes around, whether that's for getting in or for seeding.Where to watch Bengals-Jaguars liveDate: Sunday, Oct. 4 | Time: 1 p.m. ETLocation: Paycor Stadium (Cincinnati, OH)TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Bengals -2.5 (via DraftKings)Jaguars-Bengals need to know:Bengals defense: Cincinnati's defense was by far its weak spot last season, but this year the unit has improved a lot — except for last week. It had its worst showing of the season in the loss and needs to step it up this week against a Jaguars offense that seems to be building confidence by the week. 
Jags defense vs. Chase, Higgins: Tee Higgins ranks ninth in receiving yards through three games (244), while Chase ranks 27th (185). The Jaguars defense allowed Jaylen Waddle to have a 100-yard game last week and have a challenge ahead of them to stop the WR duo. Jacksonville did a good job shutting down Patriots receivers last week, only allowing 178 passing yards and no touchdowns. Plus, they stopped all three red zone tries. Burrow vs. Lawrence by the numbers: Burrow has a 70.9 completion percentage (sixth most), 743 yards (12th most ), six touchdowns, one interception and seven sacks taken. Lawrence has a 66.7 completion percentage, 616 yards, seven touchdowns, two interceptions and four sacks taken. The Jaguars could work on their passing game, but they have a stronger run game than their Week 4 opponent. Both quarterbacks are playing at a high level so far, so this battle should be a fun one to watch. These two have a history as well. They faced each other in the 2020 National Championship, when Burrow's LSU defeated Lawrence's Clemson.Jaguars-Bengals prediction:I think this one could be close, but I think the Jaguars will take it. They look like one of the teams to beat in the AFC, and I think they will continue their winning streak against the Bengals.
Pick: Jaguars

The most surprising part of Cal's early-season swoon has been how pedestrian the offense has looked in quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele's sophomore campaign. JKS was one of college football's top freshmen a year ago, but the Golden Bears' new coaching staff has yet to unlock his best in 2026. The Tigers, despite a 16-8 record against AP-ranked opponents at home under Dabo Swinney, find themselves as heavy underdogs to Mario Cristobal's Hurricanes, and hope to use this stage to reaffirm their place as an ACC contender. Miami and Clemson are the only two teams with a 2-0 record in ACC play, so this makes Saturday's game a battle for solo first place in the standings. That's exactly where Miami expected to be as a top-five team with national title aspirations, but it's also been an elusive goal during 22 years of conference membership. While Miami has had great seasons since joining the league in 2004, including reaching the national championship game last season, it has yet to win the ACC Championship in football and has only played in the title game once. The opponent in that one ACC Championship Game was against Dabo Swinney and Clemson in 2017, with the Hurricanes being the third of six consecutive teams to lose to the Tigers in Charlotte.  The all-time series between these two national title-winning programs is split dead even at 7-7, with each team winning half of their games at home (8 at Miami, 4 at Clemson) and each team winning one of the two neutral-site meetings.

title: 2026 WNBA playoffs: Grading every team in the first round - CBS Sports
description: The first round of the 2026 WNBA playoffs came to a close on Friday with another thriller between the Golden State Valkyries and Dallas
body:
The first round of the 2026 WNBA playoffs came to a close on Friday with another thriller between the Golden State Valkyries and Dallas Wings. The Valkyries fell behind by 16 points in the middle of the third quarter, but pulled off a stunning comeback to take the do-or-die Game 3 and earn the first playoff series victory in franchise history. The Valkyries will now face the reigning champion Las Vegas Aces, who outlasted the Indiana Fever in their own three-game series. On the other side of the bracket, the New York Liberty, who knocked off the No. 1 seed Minnesota Lynx, will face the Atlanta Dream, who swept the Washington Mystics. The semifinals will start on Sunday with Game 1 of both series. Before the postseason continues, let's take one final look back at the first round and hand out grades for all eight teams. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York Liberty: A+By the time the playoffs rolled around, just about everyone outside of Brooklyn had given up on the Liberty, who had sunk all the way to the No. 8 seed amid another frustrating, injury-filled season. And then, all of a sudden, the team we'd been waiting for all season finally showed up. 
The Liberty didn't just beat the Lynx; they thoroughly embarrassed them en route to becoming the first No. 8 seed to beat a No. 1 seed in a first-round series. Their size, length and physicality was overwhelming, as they made Olivia Miles look like an actual rookie for the first time all season, and trailed for just three minutes and 23 seconds across the two games. New York was one of two teams to complete a first-round sweep, and did so while winning both games by 16. Breanna Stewart was sensational, particularly in Game 1, when she recorded the fourth 30-point, 10-rebound, five-assist playoff game in WNBA history, and she got plenty of help. Crucially, even from Sabrina Ionescu, who has not been herself after returning from injury this season. Ionescu had 18 points and seven assists in Game 2, and shot 7 of 18 from 3-point range (38.9%) in the series. If Ionescu can be even close to her usual self, that completely changes the Liberty's fortunes. The Liberty have the worst odds (+430, per FanDuel) to win the title, but none of the four teams still remaining had a better showing in the first round. 

        
            
                Liberty oust Lynx from playoffs: How Minnesota became first No. 1 seed slayed by a No. 8 seed in WNBA history
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Atlanta Dream: A-The Dream's first-round series against the Mystics wasn't pretty, but it was never going to be given those two teams' styles. Amid an absurd amount of physicality, the Dream proved once again that they're one of the toughest teams in the league and won't go down without a fight. DeWanna Bonner, who only played five regular-season games with the Dream after arriving in late August, showed the value of her playoff experience by taking over the third quarter of Game 1 to flip that game on its head and turn a double-digit deficit into a 17-point win. Their Game 2 win was much more comprehensive, though they once again showed strong character by fighting off a late Mystics rally. Playing the Mystics helped on this front, of course, but no team had a better defensive showing in the first round. They forced 26 steals, blocked nine shots and held Washington to 39.7% shooting. Defensive Player of the Year Angel Reese, in her first season with the Dream and first-ever playoff series, was a big part of their success on that end, as were Rhyne Howard and Jordin Canada. 
This was the Dream's first multi-game playoff series victory since 2013 (they won a single-elimination "series" in 2016) and snapped a streak of three consecutive first-round exits. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Las Vegas Aces: BThe Aces' ability to find a way to win is truly remarkable and was on display yet again in Game 3 against the Fever. After leading by 12 in the second half, they found themselves up by just two with less than three minutes to play. From that point, they outscored the Fever 12-3 to advance to the semifinals and continue their repeat quest. All 12 of those points were scored by their Big Three of A'ja Wilson, Jackie Young and Chelsea Gray, which was fitting considering that trio was responsible for 213 of their 285 points (74.7%) and 47 of their 56 assists (83.9%) in the series. There are few players you'd rather have than those three in a big moment, but can they actually repeat with that trio carrying such a burden? 
The Aces got the job done, but once again were not entirely convincing in the process. Dating back to the start of the 2025 playoffs, this was the third time in four series that they were pushed to the brink. Last season, they needed a game-winner from Young in Game 3 of the first round, and went to overtime in Game 5 of the semifinals. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Valkyries: B-The Valkyries' first playoff series victory in franchise history could not have come in more dramatic fashion. After falling behind by 16 in the third quarter of Game 3, amid a scoreless drought that lasted nearly seven minutes and included 15 consecutive missed shots, the Valkyries stormed back to beat the Wings. Gabby Williams played hero with the go-ahead bucket in the final 90 seconds and clutch free throws to seal the win. It's funny how playoff series go, and how perception can swing in a matter of days. The Valkyries dominated Game 1 and, if not for a few miraculous shots by Arike Ogunbowale in Game 2, would have swept the series and felt great going into the semis. Instead, they were forced into a winner-take-all Game 3 and their offense, which has been a concern all season long, had the type of showing everyone had been dreading. 
The Valkyries did get the job done in the end, but their vaunted defense was not at its best for the majority of the series, and Game 3 was a stark reminder of the issues they can have on offense, especially when their 3-pointers -- which they take more often than any other team -- aren't going in. 
        
            
                'A switch flipped': Valkyries erase 16-point deficit against Wings, advance to WNBA semis to face the Aces
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Wings: C+Heading into the playoffs, the consensus was that Valkyries vs. Wings was the most straightforward of the four first-round series. No one gave the Wings, who were just 7-14 against playoff teams this season, a chance. And when they trailed by as much as 36 in Game 1 en route to a 24-point loss, it seemed an uneventful sweep was indeed in order. And then Arike Ogunbowale showed up. She sent Game 2 to overtime with a remarkable 3-pointer from deep in the corner and single-handedly won that contest for the Wings with the highest scoring playoff game in WNBA history: 45 points. She poured in another 30 points in Game 3, and may have completed the upset if it wasn't for an apparent groin injury late in the fourth quarter that caused her to briefly leave the game. 
The Wings' first playoff appearance since 2023 certainly wasn't perfect. They were crushed in Game 1, Paige Bueckers was limited to 27 points on 27 shots in the final two games and they blew a 16-point lead in the second half of Game 3. But they put up a much better fight than anyone expected from them, and they had one of the title favorites on the ropes. There's a lot for the Wings to be proud of after that showing. 
        
            
                WNBA playoffs winners and losers: Wings' Arike Ogunbowale wows with playoff-record 45 points to force Game 3
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Indiana Fever: CFor the second consecutive season, the Fever took the Aces to the limit. And for a second consecutive season, they came up short. This time, it was in the first round, which is certainly discouraging considering they entered the season with championship expectations. In many ways, the Fever's first-round series was a microcosm of their season. They were much better at home, which they showed in Game 2, and when Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell had things rolling, their offense was unstoppable. But their defense was not good enough, they had no reliable depth, particularly in the frontcourt, and when a team could take one or both of their star guards out of the game, they didn't have enough answers. 
In Game 1, Clark and Mitchell had 27 points on 33 shots. In Game 2, they had 53 points on 34 shots. And in Game 3, they had 41 points on 41 shots. The Fever were within two in the final three minutes of a winner-take-all Game 3 on the road against the reigning champs. This series wasn't a disaster for them, but it did reiterate the fact that they're a few pieces away from actually winning a title. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Washington Mystics: C-Just getting to the playoffs -- their first appearance since 2023 -- was a major success for the Mystics, who are officially ahead of schedule with their rebuild. With an average age of 24 years, the Mystics were both the youngest team in the league this season and the youngest team in league history to make the postseason. That youth was on display in the first round against the Dream, as was their lack of juice on the offensive end. They fell apart in the second half of Game 1 on the road. And then, after cutting a double-digit deficit down to three early in the fourth quarter at home, they immediately gave up a 13-0 run that ended the game. In two games, the Mystics shot 50 of 126 (39.7%) from the field, including 13 of 41 (31.7%) from 3-point range, and had 41 turnovers to 26 assists. 
The series was more competitive than the final margins -- 15 points in Game 1 and 18 points in Game 2 -- would indicate, and it's hard to be too harsh on a team that had eight rookies and so little playoff experience. Still, getting swept was disappointing given how well the Mystics were playing entering the playoffs. After the All-Star break, they were 14-4, which was tied for the best record in the league -- ironically, with the Dream. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota Lynx: FWhat a disaster for the Lynx, who became not only the first No. 1 seed to lose a first-round series to a No. 8 seed under the league's new playoff format, but the first No. 1 seed to lose a first-round game to a No. 8 seed. And sure, the Liberty -- the preseason title favorites -- weren't a typical No. 8 seed. The seven games separating the two teams in the regular season standings was the smallest gap between the No. 1 and No. 8 seeds in the decade that the league has been taking the top-eight teams regardless of conference. 
But that excuse would have carried more weight if the Lynx hadn't been totally outclassed. They led for just three minutes and 23 seconds and lost each game by 16. Unanimous Rookie of the Year Olivia Miles had 16 points on 4 of 20 shooting with two assists and five turnovers, before being benched for good, and their vets weren't much better. McBride and Williams shot a combined 20 of 54 (37%) and Collier averaged just 13 points per game on 42.9% shooting.

        We may see a fast riser emerge in the Heisman Trophy race after this week's schedule of college football games when No. 5 Ohio State plays its first Big Ten road game at No. 14 Iowa.  The Hawkeyes are flying sky-high after Hank Brown's last-second touchdown pass defeated Michigan in the Big House last week. The task is tougher this week. Legendary Iowa coach Kirk Ferentz called Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith one of the best players of the last 20 years this week. In the SEC, No. 7 Alabama and No. 16 Mississippi State hook up in Starkville for a noon ET kickoff featuring two quarterbacks who have captured the nation's attention in just a few short weeks. Mississippi State's Kamario Taylor, who already owns two road wins and a 2-0 SEC start with a victory over top-25 Missouri, has risen to third in the Heisman odds. Nipping at his heels is Alabama's Keelon Russell, who leads the nation's fourth-best scoring offense at 48 points per game. The winner Saturday might solidify himself as the third-best player in the odds.  Meanwhile, No. 8 Florida travels to No. 25 Missouri. The Gators have been among the more physical teams in the country, but how do they respond after thrashing top-10 Ole Miss last week? Mizzou has notoriously struggled against ranked opponents, even at home.  
Auburn heads to Knoxville to face No. 17 Tennessee following a chaotic week marked by the arrest of an Auburn staff member accused of leaking recruiting materials to rival programs. Amid the off-field controversy, Auburn coach Alex Golesh will aim to beat his former mentor, Volunteers coach Josh Heupel. No. 11 BYU hits the road for its first Big 12 road game against TCU, with whispers about Sonny Dykes' future in Fort Worth in the background. Bill Belichick gets another chance to build on his progress against No. 3 Notre Dame as the Irish come to North Carolina for a noon kickoff Saturday.  Then there are the coaches on the hot seat needing big wins. South Carolina's Shane Beamer hosts No. 24 Kentucky in perhaps the biggest game of his career (and without pass rusher Dylan Stewart, whom he suspended for insubordination). No. 6 Indiana hits the road for the first time at Rutgers after struggling to put away Northwestern last week, but are Greg Schiano's Scarlet Knights equipped to challenge the Hoosiers?  The Future vs. The Past matchup between Mario Cristobal's Miami and Dabo Swinney's Clemson is another of the week's more interesting narratives. Clemson has never been this large of an underdog in Swinney's tenure.  
Here are the picks from our CBS Sports experts. description: Ben Johnson turns back to his primary backup over veteran Case Keenum, who threw two touchdowns in a shocking ups
body:
Ben Johnson turns back to his primary backup over veteran Case Keenum, who threw two touchdowns in a shocking upset over the Eagles on Monday night
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Chicago Bears have reportedly made a decision on their starting quarterback with Caleb Williams still sidelined by a hamstring strain. The Athletic reports that Tyson Bagent will take over under center on Sunday when Chicago hosts the New York Jets. Bagent was always viewed as the Bears' backup quarterback, but the veteran Case Keenum was forced to step in when Bagent spent most of last week in concussion protocol. The 38-year-old Keenum registered one of the most shocking upsets of this young season, as he threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns in the 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night. His performance made it a legitimate question of who would start in Week 4, but head coach Ben Johnson is going back to his original second-stringer. "We'll have a discussion as a coaching staff, and we'll see where we need to go from here," Johnson said earlier this week. "But I said it last week, and I'll say it again. There was a reason why Tyson ended training camp as our No. 2 quarterback."The Bears will become the third team to ever start three different quarterbacks through the first four weeks of the season, and the first since the 1997 Jacksonville Jaguars, per CBS Sports Research. 
Bagent found his way to the Bears in 2023 after going undrafted out of Shepherd University -- a Division II school in Shepherdstown, West Virginia. He did enough in his first preseason to earn a spot on the final 53-man roster, and ended up making four starts as a rookie!In Week 7 that year, Bagent won his first career start against the Las Vegas Raiders by throwing for 162 yards and one touchdown. He then lost back-to-back starts against the Los Angeles Chargers and New Orleans Saints before defeating No. 1 overall pick Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers in prime time, 16-13. 
Bagent hasn't made a start since his wild rookie season, but did earn a two-year, $10 million extension with the Bears prior to the 2025 campaign. It made him the first Bears quarterback to sign a contract extension since Jay Cutler did so in January 2014, according to The Athletic. Now, he has a chance to earn Chicago its third win of the season.

The Bulldogs came from behind to stun No. 19 Missouri 31-24 behind 360 yards and three touchdowns from superstar quarterback Kamario Taylor. Alabama has dominated the matchup between these two teams all-time, holding an 86-18-3 advantage, including a 40-17 win in 2023. title: Who is Jalon Daniels? Meet the Buccaneers rookie QB, who went from undrafted to starting - CBS Sports
description: The undrafted Kansas product makes franchise history as he steps in for an injured Baker Mayfield with Tampa Bay
body:
The undrafted Kansas product makes franchise history as he steps in for an injured Baker Mayfield with Tampa Bay searching for its first win
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 3, 2026
                            
                    at
    1:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield is expected to miss several weeks after dislocating the thumb on his throwing hand during the Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. That means it's Jalon Daniels time in Tampa.The undrafted rookie out of Kansas will be thrown into the starting lineup this Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. He will become the first Kansas quarterback to start a game since Frank Seurer in 1987, and is actually the first undrafted rookie quarterback to start a game in Buccaneers history, per CBS Sports Research. The Bucs have gotten off to a disappointing 0-3 start, and there's plenty of blame to go around for the issues with this team. With head coach Todd Bowles on what feels like an increasingly warmer seat, can this undrafted player come in and spark the offense against a beatable opponent? Let's take a look at who Jalon Daniels is.Three-star recruit from CaliforniaDaniels was born in Lawndale, California, and attended Lawndale High School. As a recruit, 247Sports ranked him as a three-star prospect, the No. 61 dual-threat athlete in the country, and No. 298 overall player from the state of California. Daniels initially committed to Middle Tennessee State, but later decommitted and pledged allegiance to the Jayhawks.
True freshman starterDaniels was one of three Kansas quarterbacks who appeared during the season opener in 2020, which was played in an empty stadium due to the coronavirus pandemic. He got the start for his second collegiate game, and completed 19 of 33 passes for 159 yards while also rushing for 23 yards in a 47-14 loss to Baylor. Daniels was just 17 years old at the time. It was a tough season for Daniels and the Jayhawks, as Kansas finished with a 0-9 record. The true freshman completed 50% of his passes for 718 yards, one touchdown and four interceptions in seven games played with six starts. 
                                                                    Getty Images
                                                            Back to backup, then a memorable first winKansas named Jason Bean its new starting quarterback for the 2021 season, but an injury forced Daniels back into the lineup. That first start came against the hated Texas Longhorns -- who were around 30-point favorites against Kansas. Daniels led the Jayhawks to a thrilling 57-56 upset victory in overtime, in which he threw for 202 yards, three touchdowns, and rushed for 45 yards and another touchdown. 
Daniels showed off his ability as a magician on the game-winning two-point conversion. 
Rock Chalk roller coasterDaniels was named the starter for the 2022 season, which was his junior year. Kansas started hot, winning its first five games before eventually falling to a ranked TCU team. Overall, the Jayhawks tallied their most victories in a single season (6) since 2008, while Daniels threw for 2,014 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions.Entering 2023, Daniels was named the Big 12 Preseason Offensive Player of the Year. The college football world was prepared to embrace him as the lovable legend of Lawrence, but a nagging back injury suffered prior to the start of the campaign held Daniels to just three games. Even without Daniels, Kansas went 9-4 and won its first bowl game in 15 years. Running back Devin Neal emerged as a star, rushing for 1,280 yards and 16 touchdowns that year.
Daniels announced on Nov. 16, 2023, that he would be returning to Kansas for what would be his redshirt junior season in 2024. "I'm going to be blunt. This season didn't go as planned," Daniels said. "But life comes at you fast, and sometimes your story's out of your control. But I guess that just means I have unfinished business. My dreams haven't changed, my goals are still there, and my vision for my future is clear. So you want something to talk about? Talk about this: I'm not done yet, and I'm not going anywhere. Rock Chalk."Kansas had a rough start to the year, losing six of its first eight games. However, the Jayhawks rebounded to beat three ranked teams in a row in Iowa State, BYU and Colorado. Daniels threw for 2,454 yards, 14 touchdowns and a career-high 12 interceptions, but also recorded a career-high 439 yards rushing and six touchdowns. 
Daniels then returned for his sixth year at Kansas thanks to COVID-19 and injury waivers."It's all about finishing where you started," Daniels told CBS Sports prior to the 2025 season. "I went to multiple high schools. I went to multiple middle schools. Kansas gave me a chance when no other Power Five school in the nation gave me a chance, and I feel like that has a big part to do with it."Daniels registered his second-straight 5-7 season, and threw for a career-high 2,531 yards, a career-high 22 touchdowns and seven interceptions. 
"My Kansas journey has kind of been just like my life; it's come with a lot of ups and downs, and it hasn't been easy at all," Daniels said. "When I felt like I've been performing at my greatest, trials and tribulations such as injuries have come about. It's always just been about being able to bounce back from it."NFL journey beginsDaniels' Kansas story didn't go or end how everyone wanted it to. While he flashed star potential, he left Lawrence with a 19-26 record and questions about his future as a football player. Daniels finished his collegiate career ranked second in program history in passing yards (9,282) and passing touchdowns (67), and was one of two Jayhawks to ever accumulate 10,000 yards of total offense, joining Todd Reesing. Draft pundits criticized his throwing mechanics, accuracy, and ability to diagnose coverages, but what he could do as a scrambler was enticing. It all led to Daniels going undrafted, but he found an opportunity with the Buccaneers.
In Tampa, Mayfield was established as the starter, and he had Jake Browning as a new No. 2. Browning was once viewed as a top backup in the NFL, as he won four of seven starts with the Cincinnati Bengals in 2023. However, Daniels found a way to unseat him. The rookie completed 61.4% of his passes for 239 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in three preseason games played and also rushed for 37 yards and another touchdown. Now, Daniels is presented with a massive opportunity. From being an underrated recruit out of California, to the ups and downs at Kansas and his victorious fight to earn a roster spot on an NFL team, Daniels can add another chapter to his already-fascinating story by registering an upset victory in his first NFL start. Who's to say it's not possible? Quarterbacks who did not start Week 1 are a perfect 6-0. "I think that one thing I learned in college was, you can't be the thermometer, you have to be the thermostat," Daniels said this week. "You have to be someone who comes in and is able to set the temperature of the room, not test the room and try to be able to blend in with it. If a team is low, I have to be able to pick it up to be able to make sure that they're even. If we're high, then I have to be able to be low to be able to make sure that we're even. I try to be as even-keel as possible. I think that being able to go out there and have that even-keeled feel, the team around you feels that."
